newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Technihire drops after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Technihire drops after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in South African firm Technihire Ltd fell on Friday after the firm warned on potential losses from significant debtors.
The firm's stock dropped 38.0 percent, or 36 cents, to 58 cents by 0736 GMT -- making it the biggest loser in percentage terms on the bourse in early trade.

Technihire, which is a technical personnel hire firm, said that the potential losses, which appear to be due to fraudulent activity, would reduce capital and consequent loan funding required resulting in losses exceeding the net asset value of the firm.
"It is taking a big hit after that announcement. There seems to be a lot wrong with the firm," one dealer said.

The firm said that Adecco SA, its ultimate holding company, had issued a guarantee of 10 million rand to ensure the trading ability of the firm remins unimparied. However, it would take time to restore the company to profitability and recapitalisation will be necessary.
As part of its global restructuring and as a result of the current situation, Adecco was in talks regarding a restructuring or possible delisting of the firm.
An offer to minorities of 50 cents a share was being considered.
